assessment.reason: Under 1.5 shots at +130 clears break-even in both scaled scenarios, and the settlement basis is published. No supplied evidence directly undercuts it. The margin is thin and unvalidated.
assessment.model_case: The projection is a mean of 1.73 shots and a median of 2 on 17.0 minutes, and the under needs zero or one shot. The case rests on dispersion around a mean above the line. Scaling volume up a tenth leaves it only marginally above break-even.
assessment.price_case: Main 1.5 line at +130 against a model minimum near +129, so the quote barely clears. Three other books price near break-even. The blended view is only slightly above it, so a small price drop removes the case.
assessment.context_case: There is no Strome-specific reporting. Philadelphia defensive absences and a back-to-back could lift Washington shot volume, a modest headwind for the under.

qualitative_review.countercase: A mean above the line already favors two or more shots. If Strome gets added power-play time or faces a tired, depleted Flyers defense, the shot volume behind the under could rise and erase the thin margin.

assessment.reason: With a projected mean near 0.29 assists and a median of zero, the under is the likely outcome. The model case stays above break-even across the supplied sensitivity range. The price is steep, so the margin rests on the model's estimate rather than on a large structural mismatch.
assessment.model_case: At about 16.8 projected minutes with a shrunk assist rate, a no-assist game is the base case. Assist outcomes are less sensitive to minor role shifts than shot volume. The weakness is power-play assignment: an unverified promotion would lift the assist rate.
assessment.price_case: This is a main-line quote at -190, requiring about 65.5 in 100. Only one other book quotes it, which is not broad consensus. The model clears break-even even at the low end of sensitivity, but the market-weighted blend barely exceeds it. Do not treat this as independent of the Kapanen candidate in the same game.
assessment.context_case: The player does not appear in the injury table, which does not establish health. A day-to-day Edmonton winger could alter deployment if this player is an Oiler. No player-specific reporting was supplied, so context is unverified.

qualitative_review.countercase: At -190, the payout is thin, and a single secondary assist loses. If the player moves onto a top unit or first power-play group, the assist rate could rise enough to erase the margin. Thin book coverage means the price may not reflect a sharp consensus.
